ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
The diagram shows two circles and a square with sides of length $10 \mathrm{~cm}$. One vertex of the square is at the centre of the large circle and two sides of the square are tangents to both circles. The small circle touches the large circle. The radius of the small circle is $(a-b \sqrt{2}) \mathrm{cm}$.
<image1>
What is the value of $a+b$ ?

Reasoning: Establish a coordinate system according to the specified method, set the center of the large circle, that is, the lower-left vertex of the square, as the origin, and the square extends to the right and upward. The side length of the square is 10, so the right side is x=10, and the upper side is y=10. Since the distances from the center of the large circle to these two tangent lines are both 10, the radius of the large circle is 10. Let the radius of the small circle be r. The small circle is tangent to both x=10 and y=10, and is at the upper-right corner, so the center of the small circle is (10-r, 10-r). In the figure, the small circle and the large circle are externally tangent, therefore the distance between the two centers is equal to 10+r. r(√2 + 1) = 10√2 - 10 = 10(√2 - 1)。
所以：
r = 10(√2 - 1)/(√2 + 1) = 10(3 - 2√2) = 30 - 20√2。
